title.narrative: EngenderHealth SRHR (Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights) Burkina Faso
EngenderHealth SRHR (Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter) Burkina Faso

description.narrative: EngenderHealth, project aims to expand access to quality abortion care and reduce unintended pregnancies among vulnerable populations and in humanitarian settings in Burkina Faso.

EngenderHealth, projektet syftar till att öka tillgången till kvalitativ abortvård och minska antalet oavsiktliga graviditeter bland utsatta befolkningsgrupper och i humanitära situationer i Burkina Faso.

The project aims to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality associated with unsafe abortion and increase the ability of women, including adolescent girls and young women, particularly those who are internally displaced and living in host communities, to realize their bodily autonomy. This will be done through four mutually reinforcing objectives: 1.Create a sustainable advocacy environment and a strong movement for quality safe abortion and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) 2.Improve the policy, legal, and strategic environment to advance quality abortion care 3.Increase the agency of women and adolescents to prevent unintended pregnancies and access quality abortion care 4.Improve availability of quality, integrated comprehensive abortion care (CAC), family planning (FP), and gender-based violence (GBV) services for underserved and displaced populations

description.narrative: Objective 1: Create a sustainable advocacy environment and a strong movement for quality abortion care and SRH Three key strategies drive the achievement of this objective: •Wide stakeholder collaboration and a thorough analysis of the abortion ecosystem to support local actors in the creation of a movement for quality abortion. This is to be followed by the development of the first ever National Plan for Quality Abortion Care. •Strengthen the capacity of duty bearers (e.g. opinion leaders, parliament) at national level and in the 5 regions supported on the policy, legislative regulatory context that supports quality abortion care. •Increase knowledge and access to information to rights holders through mass media approaches (e.g., regional radio broadcasts and other means). Objective 2: Improve the policy, legal, and strategic environment to advance quality abortion care •Agreement on areas where laws, policies and regulations are inconsistent and enhance knowledge and confidence among providers and policy makers to extend safe abortion services •Identification and agreement on key technical areas that can be expanded in years four & five (such as self-managed abortion, task shifting, liberalization of legal and regulatory barriers) •WHO guideline and core components rolled out •The Family Life Education Curriculum rolled out Objective 3: Women and adolescents can exercise their agency to prevent unintended pregnancies and access to quality abortion care Three core strategies will be used to address these challenges and build on the considerable assets that exist within communities: •Providing technical support to youth organizations such as SOS/JD and other local organizations to engage community members in the catchment areas on gender transformative community dialogues that can create positive attitudes for accessing safe abortion care, contraception, and GBV. •Strengthening young peoples access to information and knowledge of SRH and access to RH services in communities and directly working with one school per region and with out of school youth. •Removing barriers to access to contraception and safe abortion services by piloting a community network of trusted aunties to support AGYW with information and referral to facilities and support of transport costs through a voucher system. Objective 4: The availability of quality, integrated CAC, FP, and GBV services for underserved and displaced populations is improved Four key strategies drive the achievement of this objective: •Training of 180 health providers in the first three years and an additional 70 providers trained in years 4-5 in delivering quality and non-discriminatory access to quality abortion care and contraceptive and SGBV services, within the context of current health provisions and regulations. •Procurement in consultation with the ministry to ensure limited/no stockouts of medical equipment and supplies in the project region. •Extension of training to village birth attendants and CHWs to prevent deaths related to pregnancy in areas where health facilities have closed due to insecurity. •Targeted approaches to address discrimination and stigma through the expansion of VCAT training.
